editorial.subjectLine: Twelve teams, two days, one AI hackathon
editorial.previewText: The venue prize went to kailine — and on 3 September we're at Les Mills Auckland City for the next one.

founderNote.heading: A note from our founder
founderNote.bodyMd:
We opened the Aotearoa AI Hackathon Festival on Friday 7 August in the Sir Paul Reeves Building at AUT City Campus. By Saturday morning the wall outside the team rooms was covered in hand-written sheets, a team name and an idea on each one. The one I keep thinking about read: "AI-based form-fill assistant for visually impaired people".

Twelve teams pitched on Saturday afternoon in WG308, five minutes each, to a judging panel that had to take in a dozen unfamiliar ideas in one sitting. The venue prize went to kailine, with kaitiakidata and kpi-kaitiaki-positive-impact as runners-up. That winning pitch, recorded on the day, now goes to the national panel, and the national finalists pitch at the [Aotearoa AI Summit](https://aotearoaai.nz) in Wellington on 8–9 September.

What stays with me is how ordinary it looked by the end. People who had not met before Friday evening stood up together on Saturday and explained something they had built in two days. That is the whole reason we keep putting these rooms together.
founderNote.signature: Dr. Mahsa McCauley, Founder & Chair, She Sharp

headline.blurb: An evening at Les Mills Auckland City on diversity and AI for impact: a cross-functional panel, table discussions, and enough time afterwards to actually meet the people in the room.

photoOfTheMonth.caption: The winning team, kailine, on stage at AUT City Campus as the venue result went up behind them.

editorial.recapIntro: August was a single event that filled two whole days — here is how it went at AUT.

eventBlurbs.aotearoa-ai-hackathon-festival-2026: Twelve teams took on the AI for Good brief across Friday evening and all of Saturday, then pitched for five minutes each to a local judging panel. kailine won the venue prize, ahead of kaitiakidata and kpi-kaitiaki-positive-impact.

opportunities.title: Become a mentor
opportunities.body: The mentors at the hackathon did not build anything for anyone. They asked better questions, and teams got unstuck. That is most of the job, and a few hours a month is enough to do it.

opportunities.title: Volunteer with us
opportunities.body: Two days at AUT ran on people who set up rooms, kept the kai coming, and noticed the person standing on their own. September's panel is the next one that needs you.

opportunities.title: Support the mahi
opportunities.body: Our events are free to attend, which is a decision someone has to pay for. A donation of any size keeps the door open for the next person walking through it.

editorial.sponsorThanks: Two days at AUT City Campus took a lot of people. Thank you to AUT for the building and the rooms, to AI Forum New Zealand for running the festival nationally, and to AWS behind the prizes. Thank you also to Fisher & Paykel Healthcare, Woolworths New Zealand with Kai Commitment, and My Life My Voice for putting real problems in front of the teams, and to Seen Ventures for the free Hack Fit training in the weeks beforehand.

newsBites.title: ShadowTech26 Opens Doors for 1,500 Girls
newsBites.summary: Tech Women’s ShadowTech26 programme is back, providing over 1,500 secondary school girls across Aotearoa the chance to explore tech careers this August. This initiative aims to inspire young women in Years 9–11 by connecting them with local tech workplaces.

newsBites.title: Women Underrepresented in AI Roles
newsBites.summary: Despite a boom in AI jobs, women hold just 13% of C-suite AI leadership roles, according to LinkedIn research across 27 countries. This highlights ongoing gender disparities in the tech industry.

newsBites.title: Job ads fell for a third month, Auckland included
newsBites.summary: July saw a 0.8% decline in job ads across New Zealand, marking three consecutive months of falling numbers. In Auckland, job ads dropped 0.9% m/m, with significant declines in industries like Sales and Manufacturing.

didYouKnow.text: 60% of New Zealand's top 200 tech companies are based in Auckland — chances are the one you want to work for is just down the road.
